speaker: Doctor
text: That is an unusual combination of symptoms for a wrist injury. To help me understand your condition better, can you tell me how long you have had the fever and skin lesions? Also, do you have a history of any recent insect bites or animal scratches?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; the camping trip in Minnesota and the recent knee pain are significant clues. Given the combination of fever, wrist pain, and skin lesions, have you noticed any rash specifically on your palms or soles, or any joint swelling? Additionally, when did you last have sexual contact with your partner, and have you seen a doctor for the knee pain yet?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Lyme Disease (Erythema Migrans and Lyme Arthritis).

Based on the history of camping in Minnesota, recent knee pain, and the specific description of violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on the wrists, I suspect a tick-borne illness like Lyme disease rather than an infectious arthritis from a bite. REQUEST TEST: Serologic testing for Borrelia burgdorferi (ELISA followed by Western Blot). REQUEST IMAGES: Full-body photograph to check for Erythema Migrans rash.
